attacks.unsupported_mechanism: KILLED - claimed 85% viability reduction across "all size fractions" via PEF, but the candidate's own known_failure_modes list "large metazoans shielded by their own body size," which physically precludes the claimed uniform efficacy across size fractions (membrane permeabilization by 60 kV/cm pulses does not scale to organisms whose diameter exceeds the inter-electrode field uniformity zone, and PEF has no residual biocidal action during the 30 min hold — permeabilized but unlysed cells can recover viability).
attacks.obvious_combination: KILLED - PEF treatment of ballast water (e.g., the Hyde Marine/Ballast Water Treatment Systems PEF unit, commercially deployed circa 2010s) combined with a downstream holding tank for contact time is a known, well-documented combination in BWMS literature; mapping field strength and pulse count to organism size fractions is routine PEF optimization, not a novel integration.
attacks.prior_art: SURVIVE (firewall: prior_art_state=UNRESOLVED_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE is a non-kill state; adversarial PRIOR_ART=KILL is forbidden)
attacks.engineering_infeasibility: KILLED - claimed 90 kW pulsed supply delivering 60 kV pulses across a co-flow chamber at 350 m3/h; published PEF BWMS designs (e.g., Hyde, ATENA) operate at orders-of-magnitude lower specific power (~kW, not 90 kW) and 85% across-size efficacy has not been demonstrated at this flow rate — the 90 kW figure is not grounded by a corresponding chamber geometry, electrode area, or pulse repetition rate, making the power/flow pairing engineering-unspecified and infeasible as stated.
